opening.text: Book is up 17.5% — $1,446 of crypto on $1,231 deposited, and every single name is within 3% of entry or better. ZEC is the star: $939 to $1,141 in nine days, +130% on the month, and the privacy sector is the ONLY sector trading above its October 2025 Bitcoin-ATH level. Grayscale's ZEC ETF has been pulling inflows since Aug 25. DOT quietly ripped +13.4% on the week off a short squeeze and a governance vote that could cut supply. This is what a recovery tape looks like — BTC has clawed back to $77,391, +21% on the month from the June $64k bottom. Nothing here needs fixing.

Numbers, cleanly. LINK 38.04 units at $11.598 = $441 on $446 cost, -1.1%, day 14. LTC $208 on $200, +4.0%. DOT $290 on $280, +3.5%. ADA $97.66 on $100, -2.3%. NEAR $240 on $244, -1.7%. SOL $98.29 on $89.36, +10.0%. ZEC $71.04 on $59, +20.4%. The aggregate +17.5% is almost entirely ZEC and SOL carrying five roughly-flat positions — strip those two and the remaining $1,270 of cost is producing about +0.4%. Buying power is $7.14; a $100 ZEC preview was rejected outright by Robinhood. There is no trade to make today regardless of what the lenses say.

BTC dominance is 58.2% and drifting toward the 60% line where alts start bleeding outright. Global market cap printed -4.2% on 24 hours while our names moved -1% or less — that dispersion means capital is leaving somewhere else fast, and diffusion tends to arrive late, not never. LINK is the live problem: fourteen days held, flat, and it touched $13.64 on September 8 before surrendering the whole move. I am overriding the dead-money sell because the catalyst stack is real — Coinbase named Chainlink the oracle for tokenized US equities on Base, Schwab is adding LINK, the Bottomline SWIFT deal landed — but that override has an expiry. If LINK is not above +5% by September 19 it goes, catalysts or not. DOT also still carries the Hyperbridge exploit overhang and sits a rounding error above an all-time low.

Everyone is reading +17.5% as skill. It is one coin. ZEC at +2,496% off the lows with a fresh ETF and 'privacy is the trade of the year' headlines in Motley Fool is not an entry signal — it is the sound made at the top of a sector rotation. Fear and Greed at 63 with BTC still 39% below its all-time high is the market pricing a recovery it has not earned; the 2026 crash was institutional — ETF redemptions, basis unwinds, MicroStrategy selling coin for the first time — and none of that structurally reversed. The contrarian read: the flat names are the honest ones. DOT at 98% below ATH and ADA at 93% below are where the asymmetry actually lives, and both are boring precisely because nobody wants them yet. If James adds cash, the disciplined move is into the ugliest position, not the prettiest.
